archetypes.name: stream-contracts
archetypes.rationale: This migration replaces three shell helpers with a Python CLI and exactly replicates their stdout/stderr/exit-code contracts; deviations are silent runtime breakage for every shell consumer.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine `python/tracking_issue.py` for stdout/stderr placement parity with the retired shell helpers. Verify that `read_main` shell-level usage failures emit `FAILED=true`/`ERROR=usage:...` on stdout (not stderr), while parser-level missing-option-value cases emit usage diagnostics on stderr only with no stdout envelope. Verify that `upsert_summary_main` non-usage failure envelopes (`FAILED=true`, `ERROR=`) route to stderr, while every other tracking-issue verb keeps non-usage failure envelopes on stdout. Verify exit code contracts: `read_main` must exit only 0, 1, or 2 (never 3); write mains must use exit 3 exclusively for compose-time secret redaction failures; `upsert_summary_main` must use exit 1 for invalid-repo and exit 3 only for secret redaction failure. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fail-closed
archetypes.rationale: Several ordering and fail-closed invariants in the new Python code guard against token leakage and silent data corruption; a single wrong branch can silently expose secrets or corrupt task output.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine `python/tracking_issue.py` for fail-closed and ordering invariants. Verify that every non-sentinel read mode validates `--out-dir` exists and is a directory before writing `task.md`, and that read cap overrides are validated before any side effect. Verify that `read_main` with `--issue --prompt` maps all delegated append failures to read exit 2 and never propagates append exit 3, and that the `append-comment failed:` prefix appears in the stdout `ERROR=` field on failure. Verify that `logging_util.quiet_init(...)` is called at the start of each CLI main before argparse can emit contract output. Verify outbound redaction order: tmpdir paths before secrets on all write paths; tmpdir redaction failure is best-effort for `upsert_summary_main` only and fail-closed for every other write verb; secret redaction failure must exit 3 on all write paths. Verify that captured `gh` stderr is sanitized through a redact-or-fallback helper before appearing in any `ERROR=` field. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: api-stability
archetypes.rationale: The public rename() function is used by finalize.py and must stay a stable string-returning adapter; any drift in the shared core or CLI dispatch wiring silently breaks library callers.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the rename design in `python/tracking_issue.py`. Verify that the public `rename(runner, issue, state, *, repo, current_title, cwd) -> str` signature is preserved exactly, delegates to the shared rename core with the caller-supplied `current_title` (no second `gh` title fetch inside public `rename()`), and returns the final title string from the core result. Verify that the shared rename core performs no KV emission and that `RENAMED=`/`NEW_TITLE=` appear only in `rename_main`. Verify that the shared core compares the prospective redacted title against the redacted canonical current title (not the raw current title) before issuing `gh issue edit`, and that `mark_false_positive` compares the marker-inserted result against the redacted title before truncation. Check `python/cli.py` to confirm all six new tracking-issue verbs (`read`, `create-issue`, `append-comment`, `rename`, `mark-false-positive`, `upsert-summary`) dispatch to the correct `*_main` functions. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
